title: What's your money personality? Take the 1-minute quiz
description: Six questions, one minute, and you'll know whether you're an avoider, a spender, a juggler or a saver, plus the one money move that suits your type. Free, no sign-up needed to see your result.
alt_text: Four cards labelled Avoider, Spender, Juggler and Saver under the question "What's your money personality?"

title: Why your budget keeps failing (it might be your money personality)
description: Some people need fewer decisions, some need guard rails, some need fewer due dates. Take the six-question quiz to find your type and the budget style that fits it.
alt_text: Headline "Your budget isn't broken. It might just be the wrong type." above four circles and a link to a one-minute quiz.

title: Budgeting apps compared honestly, including when not to pay for one
description: Six budgeting apps compared by price model, budgeting style and bank syncing, and who should skip each one. Includes the free and spreadsheet options, so you don't pay for an app you won't open.
alt_text: A comparison card listing cost, budgeting style, bank syncing and who each budgeting app is not for.

title: How to pick a high-yield savings account (and switch in 15 minutes)
description: What actually matters when you choose a high-yield savings account: deposit insurance, fees, how the rate has moved, and transfer times. Five well-known online options side by side, and the 15-minute switch.
alt_text: "Is your savings account earning almost nothing?" with a checklist: FDIC insured, no monthly fees, rate history, fast transfers.

title: Rocket Money vs YNAB vs Monarch: which budgeting app fits you?
description: Three popular budgeting apps head to head: how each one budgets, what's free, what it costs, how it handles subscriptions, couples and net worth, and who should skip each one.
alt_text: Three columns comparing Rocket Money, YNAB and Monarch under the question "Which one fits you?"

title: 0% balance transfer: do the maths before you apply
description: A balance transfer can save hundreds or cost you more. How to compare the intro period, the transfer fee and the rate afterwards, with a worked example and the mistakes that cancel out the savings.
alt_text: A large "0%" with three checks for a balance transfer: intro period, transfer fee, rate after.

title: How to budget on a $50,000 salary (2026 take-home numbers)
description: What a $50,000 salary actually leaves you each month in 2026, a line-by-line budget for it, how much rent fits, and how much your state changes the numbers. With the maths shown.
alt_text: "$50,000 a year is about $3,530 a month take-home", above a bar split into bills, funds, goals and a weekly spending number.

title: How much rent can you afford? 20 salaries, real 2026 numbers
description: The 30% rule in real dollars, plus take-home pay, a monthly plan and the big cities where a one-bedroom fits, for 20 salaries from $25,000 to $200,000.

title: 5 money kits in one: budget, bills, credit, debt and investing ($39)
description: All five Money Made Simple guide-and-spreadsheet kits in one download, with a Start Here map and a 30-day plan that uses all five. Excel, Google Sheets or Numbers. One payment, no subscription.
alt_text: The Money Made Simple Toolkit cover with five kits listed and a $39 price tag.

title: 12 printable savings challenges in one pack ($8)
description: Make saving a habit (and a bit of a game): every savings challenge from the shop in one printable pack, from the 52-week challenge to savings bingo. Letter and A4 PDFs.
alt_text: Six tiles showing printable savings challenges, including 52-week, 100 envelopes and savings bingo.
